paraphrase: Distinguishes two verification surfaces: synthesis (authored judgment like code review) vs. deterministic operations. Synthesis is inherently expensive to verify because it requires re-evaluating the judgment. Deterministic operations are cheap because the output either matches or doesn't. The high cost of verification is concentrated in the synthesis surface.

claims.text: Verification cost depends on whether the work is synthesis (authored judgment) or deterministic operation — synthesis is inherently expensive to verify
claims.notes: Appears in comments on multiple posts — consistent thesis

claims.text: A receipt for synthesis work needs different fields than a receipt for deterministic work — conflating them makes both worse
claims.notes: Implied by the distinction; not stated explicitly but follows from the argument

evaluation.notes: Key distinction that shapes the entire receipt schema design. Testable: try verifying a deterministic task vs a review task with same receipt fields.
